title: Randy's Smothered Pork Chops
imageAlt: Smothered pork chop with mushroom gravy, rice, and vegetables
summary: Bone-in chops with mushrooms, onions, and gravy. Next time: one-hour bake, creamier gravy, and mashed potatoes.
ingredients: 4 bone-in center loin pork chops, about 1 inch thick
1 large yellow onion, sliced into ¼-inch half-moons
½ cup whole milk or half-and-half
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Season the pork chops with salt and pepper.
Brown the chops in a skillet with a little butter or oil for 2–3 minutes per side. They do not need to cook through.
Remove the chops. Cook the onions for 2–3 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook another 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the cream of mushroom soup, onion soup mix, beef broth, milk, and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape up the browned bits from the skillet.
Place the chops in a baking dish, pour the gravy over them, and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 hour. Check for tenderness and doneness; add only 5–10 minutes if truly needed.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve over mashed potatoes with plenty of gravy.

journal.general: The first attempt baked for 1 hour 15 minutes and was slightly dry and tough near the bone; the outer meat was perfect. Keep the generous mushrooms and onions. There was plenty of gravy.

title: Mississippi Pot Roast
imageAlt: Mississippi pot roast served over mashed potatoes with pepperoncinis
summary: Rich, tangy chuck roast served over creamy mashed potatoes with plenty of pepperoncinis.
steps: If time allows, remove the roast from the refrigerator 20–30 minutes before cooking.
Pat the roast dry with paper towels and season lightly with black pepper. Do not add extra salt because the seasoning mixes are already salty.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the roast for 2–3 minutes per side, including the edges, until deeply browned. Do not cook it through.
Place the browned roast in the slow cooker.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning and au jus gravy mix evenly over the roast.
Place the stick of butter on top.
Add the whole pepperoncinis around the roast and pour in the pepperoncini juice.
Cover and cook on LOW until a fork slides in easily and twists the meat apart. Begin checking around 6 hours, but cook longer as needed.
If the roast is still firm late in the cook, switch to HIGH and check again after 45–60 minutes.
Shred or pull apart the tender meat and stir it into the cooking juices.
Serve over mashed potatoes with extra cooking juices and sliced pepperoncinis.

journal.general: ★★★★★ Randy Favorite. The first test used a 2.47 lb chuck roast. Cook to tenderness rather than strictly by the clock: if a fork can lift the roast without pulling it apart, it needs more time. The center became tender before the thicker outer portions, so continue cooking until all sections pull apart easily. The flavor was spot on. Next time use more pepperoncinis, add sliced pepperoncinis to each serving, and save every drop of the cooking juices for gravy and reheating leftover mashed potatoes. Served with mashed potatoes boiled exactly 18 minutes and finished with a hand mixer.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: Flavor was outstanding. The center became tender first, while the thicker outer portions needed more time. Use more pepperoncinis next time and add sliced pepperoncinis when serving.

title: Randy's Simple Mashed Potatoes
summary: Simple, creamy mashed potatoes with butter, warm milk, and sour cream.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salt for the cooking water, plus more to taste
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 2-inch chunks.
Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, and add about 1 tablespoon salt.
Bring to a boil and cook for 18–20 minutes, until a fork slides into the potatoes easily.
Drain well. Return the potatoes to the hot pot over low heat for about 1 minute to dry them slightly.
Add the butter, warm milk, and sour cream.
Mash until smooth, then season with salt and black pepper.
Stop mashing as soon as they are smooth so they do not become gluey.

journal.general: Made to serve under Mississippi Pot Roast or smothered pork chops. Excellent fresh and reheats well with a splash of milk. Even better with leftover pot roast juices or homemade gravy.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note:
Boiled exactly 18 minutes.
Butter first.
Warm milk.
Hand mixer.
Excellent.

title: Breakfast Sliders
summary: Hawaiian rolls layered with scrambled eggs, ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach, then baked until golden.
ingredients: 12 dinner rolls or Hawaiian sweet rolls
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Slice the rolls in half horizontally, keeping the tops and bottoms together as two slabs.
Place the bottom slab in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Spread the scrambled eggs evenly over the rolls, then layer on the ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach.
Place the top slab of rolls over the filling.
Brush the tops with melted butter and sprinkle with black pepper.
Bake for about 20 minutes, until the tops are golden and the cheese is melted.
Cut into 12 individual sliders and serve warm.

journal.general: La Jefa requested these again, so they are automatically a favorite. Adapted from Tasty's Breakfast Sliders recipe. Take our own photo next time and record any changes Randy and Lisa prefer.

title: Randy's Camp Breakfast Tacos
imageAlt: Camp breakfast taco on a paper plate beside a Coleman stove, with a lightly charred tortilla
summary: Built at home, finished over the campfire. Crispy tortilla, bacon, eggs, cheese, and plenty of picante.
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp. Drain and chop into bite-sized pieces.
Scramble the eggs in butter until just barely set. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Allow the bacon and eggs to cool for about 10 minutes.
Divide the eggs, bacon, and cheese evenly among the tortillas.
Roll each burrito tightly, folding the ends in as you roll.
Wrap each burrito individually in heavy-duty aluminum foil and refrigerate overnight.
At camp, indirect heat over campfire embers or a grill is preferred.
If only have a Coleman stove, place the foil-wrapped tacos on a skillet or griddle over the lowest possible flame instead of directly over the burner.
Turn every 2–3 minutes and begin checking after 8–10 minutes. Heat only until the centers are hot and the cheese is melted.
Open carefully and add plenty of picante sauce before eating.

journal.general: Designed for camping. Assemble everything at home so breakfast at camp is almost effortless. Let the eggs cool slightly before rolling so the tortillas stay firm. Heavy-duty foil works best. Picante sauce isn't optional—it gets added after opening the foil at camp.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: Coleman stove was way too hot. Tortillas burned and stuck to the foil before the centers warmed through. Next time use a skillet or griddle over the lowest flame and turn every 2–3 minutes. Lightly grease the foil or use parchment inside the foil.

title: Slow Cooker Carnitas
imageAlt: Turkey taco topped with avocado, cilantro, cotija cheese, and salsa verde, with crispy carnitas in the background
summary: Tender, flavorful slow-cooked pork finished under the broiler for crisp, browned edges.
ingredients: 1 boneless pork roast, 4–5 lb, excess fat trimmed and cut into 3-inch chunks
1 tablespoon chipotle powder, or 1 chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, minced
steps: Add the pork, beer or chicken stock, onion, garlic, chipotle, cumin, black pepper, chili powder, and salt to a large slow cooker. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6–8 hours or on HIGH for 4–5 hours, until the pork is completely tender and shreds easily with a fork.
Preheat the broiler to high. Line two large baking sheets with aluminum foil.
Shred the pork into bite-sized pieces. Use a slotted spoon to transfer it to the baking sheets, spreading it into a single even layer. Leave the cooking juices in the slow cooker.
Broil one sheet for about 5 minutes, until the edges begin to brown and crisp.
Remove the sheet from the oven, spoon about ¼ cup of the reserved cooking juices over the pork, and toss with tongs.
Broil for another 5 minutes, then spoon another ¼ cup of cooking juices over the crispy pork.
Repeat the broiling and moistening steps with the second sheet of pork.
Serve immediately in tacos, burritos, quesadillas, salads, nachos, or bowls.

journal.general: Adapted from Gimme Some Oven. The pork does not need to be seared before slow cooking because it is crisped under the broiler at the end. Save the cooking juices and add them back after each broiling step so the carnitas stay juicy. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months.

shopping: Chipotle powder or chipotle pepper in adobo sauce
Tortillas and desired toppings for serving

title: Turkey, Bacon & Avocado Sammie
imageAlt: Toasted turkey sandwich layered with melted pepper jack, crispy bacon, and avocado
summary: A hot turkey sandwich with melted pepper jack, crispy bacon, and cool avocado on toasted bread.
ingredients: About 1/2 avocado, mashed, or prepared guacamole
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp, then drain it on paper towels.
Place the sliced turkey on one slice of bread and arrange the pepper jack cheese over the turkey.
Place both bread halves in a toaster oven, keeping the plain slice separate.
Toast until the bread is golden and the pepper jack is fully melted.
Spread the mashed avocado or guacamole over the plain toasted slice.
Place the crispy bacon over the melted cheese.
Season the avocado lightly with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Close the sandwich, press gently, and serve immediately.

journal.general: Toast the sandwich open-faced so the bread gets crisp while the pepper jack melts. Add the bacon and avocado after heating so the bacon stays crisp and the avocado stays cool.

title: Creamy Italian Sausage & Potato Soup
imageAlt: Creamy Italian sausage and potato soup with spinach
summary: Creamy potato soup with sweet Italian sausage, Parmesan, and spinach. Lisa loved it; next time Randy wants less sausage.
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into bite-size pieces
3 sweet Italian sausage links, casings removed
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
2 generous handfuls fresh spinach or chopped kale
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste
½ teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
1 tablespoon butter or olive oil, only if needed for sautéing
steps: Heat a Dutch oven or soup pot over medium-high heat. Remove the sausage from the casings and cook, breaking it into bite-size chunks, until well browned, about 6–8 minutes.
Remove the sausage to a plate, leaving about 1–2 tablespoons of rendered fat in the pot. If the pot is dry, add a little butter or olive oil.
Cook the onion in the sausage drippings for 4–5 minutes, until softened and beginning to brown. Add the garlic and cook another 30–60 seconds.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir constantly for about 1 minute. Add the Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes, and black pepper.
Slowly pour in the chicken broth, stirring and scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the potatoes. Bring to a gentle boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 12–15 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Return the sausage and any accumulated juices to the pot. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the milk.
Heat gently for 5–7 minutes. Do not let the soup come to a hard boil after adding the milk. Stir in the Parmesan until melted.
Add the spinach or kale. Cook another 2–3 minutes for spinach or 4–5 minutes for kale, until wilted and tender.
Taste before salting. The sausage, chicken broth, and Parmesan may already provide enough. Adjust the black pepper, red pepper, and salt to taste.
Ladle into bowls and finish with Parmesan and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.

journal.general: First cook: used 5 sausage links instead of the recommended 3. Randy thought the sausage overpowered the soup and use 3 links next time. Lisa said, ‘It’s delicious.’ Keep this in the Maybe category for Randy, but it is La Jefa Approved. For a thicker soup, mash several potato chunks against the side of the pot near the end and stir them back in. For a brothier soup, add another ½–1 cup chicken broth. Reheat gently over medium-low heat with a splash of milk if needed.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: First cook. Used 5 sausage links. Too much sausage for me—the sausage was overpowering. Next time use 3 links. Lisa said, ‘It’s delicious.’ Maybe make again with less sausage.

title: Green Chile Chicken Enchilada Casserole
summary: Layered corn tortillas, green chile chicken, roasted poblano, Monterey Jack, crema, and Cotija. Built to freeze and reheat well.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked shredded chicken (about 1½ lb raw chicken, or meat from 1 rotisserie chicken)
1 small yellow or white onion, diced
1 can (15 oz) green enchilada sauce or about 2 cups salsa verde
¼–½ teaspoon crushed red pepper or chipotle powder, optional
1½ cups shredded Monterey Jack or Oaxaca cheese
½ cup Mexican crema or sour cream, plus more for serving
½ cup crumbled Cotija cheese, plus more for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Roast the poblano until blistered and charred in spots, turning as needed, about 10–15 minutes. Place it in a covered bowl for 5–10 minutes, then peel away loose skin, remove the stem and seeds, and dice it. Reduce the oven to 375°F.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 30–60 seconds.

Add the shredded chicken, roasted poblano, diced green chiles, cumin, Mexican oregano, black pepper, and optional red pepper or chipotle. Stir in about ¾ cup of the green enchilada sauce and ¼ cup crema. Heat for 2–3 minutes, then taste before adding any salt.
Spread a thin layer of green enchilada sauce over the bottom of an 8×8- or 9×9-inch baking dish.
Tear or cut the corn tortillas as needed to cover the bottom. Add half of the chicken mixture, about one-third of the Monterey Jack, and a light drizzle of crema.
Add another tortilla layer, the remaining chicken mixture, another third of the Monterey Jack, and another light drizzle of crema.
Finish with a final tortilla layer. Pour the remaining green enchilada sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining Monterey Jack and about ½ cup Cotija.
Cover loosely with foil and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake another 10–15 minutes, until bubbling around the edges and the Monterey Jack is melted.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting. Finish with cilantro, extra Cotija, lime, crema, and sliced jalapeño if desired.

For leftovers, cool completely and freeze individual portions in airtight containers. Thaw overnight when possible and reheat covered until hot; add a spoonful of salsa verde before reheating if it seems dry.

journal.general: First test planned for 2026-08-25. Randy already has Cotija to use. Keep the Cotija as a salty finishing cheese rather than the main melting cheese; Monterey Jack or Oaxaca provides the melted layers. Intended as a freezer-friendly casserole. Add cook notes and a photo after dinner.

shopping: Cooked shredded chicken or rotisserie chicken
Green enchilada sauce or salsa verde
